composer.available_height_rule: Clamp editor to available content height after toolbar/insets; never hide submit/stop. Expanded editor is opt-in and may require a larger window.

container_adaptation.rule: content measurement wins; no essential action hidden, overflow remains keyboard accessible

hairline_policy.note: stroke-hairline=0.5 is retained for @2x compatibility only; not a universal width
hairline_policy.split_view: Reuse decorative 1/backing_scale ink for the divider in normal contrast, stroke-rule in increased contrast. Logical divider allocation, hit slop, minimum panes and drag/cancel contract remain unchanged.

concentric.scope: Use only for declared concentric outer and inner shapes; non-concentric shapes use their own radius rule.

policy: Controls grow with text; effective minimum constraints can collapse panes before nominal breakpoints. OS windows, IME candidates and menu surfaces have OS-owned stacking.
reference_layout: OCUI proportion alignment, not a pixel-identical clone

toolbar.default_height: Toolbar row height derives from its resolved title typography and the shared Regular icon ratios. Window allocation also reserves actual native chrome overlap; system window controls keep their native size and horizontal position.
toolbar.inline: Inline and window Toolbar follow the same typography-driven size ratios; parent layout owns placement only.
toolbar.input: Painting, module viewport version/size and pointer conversion share the allocated top-region height, derived from Toolbar content and actual native chrome overlap.
toolbar.drag: Eligible native titlebar chrome may take an unhandled or explicitly bubbled primary drag; cancel the previous component interaction first and pass the retained original native mouse-down to AppKit. Captured selection/slider/splitter gestures keep ownership.
toolbar.alignment: Center Toolbar artwork and title within their typography-derived row. Genuine native traffic lights follow that same horizontal centerline through vertical-origin adjustment only; preserve native size, horizontal position, hierarchy, actions and accessibility. At extremely small text sizes native button height is the allocation floor; center the natural Toolbar row in that allocation. Apply native hit testing to the original moved controls and reapply alignment after window layout/resize. Inline Toolbar does not move window controls.
toolbar.text: Toolbar TextContent and ButtonContent labels use a single shaped line at every segment width and typography scale. Reuse the shared label ellipsis service when available; legacy string-only hosts clip an unwrapped line. Preserve full source, accessible name, mounted identity and control state. This policy does not make editor content single-line.
toolbar.typography: Application layer: resolved ui-body title typography is the Toolbar scale anchor, including host-wide zoom. Toolbar elements follow its shared ratios. System layer: native window controls retain native sizes and horizontal positions. The platform aligns only their vertical origin to the measured application Toolbar row; it never scales or replaces them.
toolbar.icons: Use the Design System Regular icon size and canonical visible-height ratio. Preserve smaller semantic marks; do not enlarge artwork to fill its SVG artboard. Align raster artwork origins to physical pixels while preserving typography-derived size and the original continuous layout/hit geometry, so translated segments retain the sampling phase.
toolbar.actions: Reuse original Button Exact frames for the computed icon box and original interaction/focus; consumers set typography only.
toolbar.splitter: Container content and its registered top Toolbar segment share the same split boundary and reflow together; segment actions compress/overflow inside that segment. Original control pointer/hover regions shield splitter paint and new input as a defensive boundary. Content retains its normal separator. Toolbar uses a short pill-ended static marker aligned to that separator with height equal to the original Toolbar icon box and the same row center; derive both from resolved Title typography and shared icon ratios; retain the marker during captured resize so it follows the shared segment boundary; recompute on every reflow and after release/cancel. Blank Toolbar padding retains the existing splitter hit width. Capture acquired before crossing controls remains with the splitter. Resolve paint, cursor regions and input from the same layout/overflow geometry for every visible column.

scroll_area.policy: Scrollbars overlay the outer padding, never content. Visibility is independent per axis and does not disable scrolling. Hidden bars have no pointer target. Shown bars appear only for overflow.

focus.clip: actual ancestor viewport only; never the control frame
focus.layout_rule: Reserve the focus paint outset around focusable content; paint outset does not enlarge hit targets.

boundary_styles.policy: Never use decorative strokes as the sole control boundary, focus or selected-state indicator. Preserve required-control contrast; distinguish noninteractive panels and preview frames.

elevation.source: DESIGN.md 2.5; floating=shadow-sm and modal=shadow-lg are project mappings; https://www.w3.org/TR/css-backgrounds-3/#shadow-blur

control_emphasis.policy: Content and primary actions lead. Named quiet actions are identified by their label/icon and transient feedback, without a resting enclosing stroke in normal or increased contrast. Required inputs and selection/error indicators retain explicit boundaries. Keyboard focus is independent. Disabled controls never paint keyboard focus.

regular.measurement: Measured canonical Regular back/forward/side-bar/side-panel vertical ink relative to their SVG artboard. This is the shared Regular layout reference; semantic small marks such as More are optical exceptions. Whole-catalog conformance is not implied.

split_view_constraints: Pane minima belong to the consumer. SplitView defaults to no content minimum; min_pane is an explicit logical-point constraint, never enlarged by a hidden percentage floor. Pointer, keyboard and resized layout honor the same requirement. If declared minima cannot fit, retain the existing constrained visible-pane behavior. Window hosts must not impose a product content minimum on behalf of a consumer.
